newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Anti-EMU motions proposed for Swedish congress.
newsitem.headline: Anti-EMU motions proposed for Swedish congress.

text.p: Sweden's ruling Social Democrats have received more motions opposed to EU economic and monetary union (EMU) membership rather than in favour of joining for its annual congress, a party spokeswoman said on Monday.
Party secretary Ingela Thalen said the majority of questions relating to EMU were saying "not now" or "wait and see".
"Many are expecting to get guidance from the ongoing committee," Thalen told a news conference.
A total of 1,826 motions were proposed for the party congress that will be held in Sundsvall in September. Of these 176 were related to EMU.
The greatest number of questions related to taxation.
The decision to come out of the congress will determine Sweden's position towards seeking to join EMU in the first round of nations from January 1, 1999.
